answer_text: A fundamental right is a basic right that a constitution epxlicitly guarantees to citizens, and which the state cannot ordinarily take away thorugh ordinary legislation, since it sits at a higher legal level than regluar laws. Because these rights are writetn into the constitution itself, courts are generally able to enforce them direclty, and a government that passes a law violating a fundamental right typically finds that law struck down thorugh judicial review. Common examples of fundamenatl rights include freedom of speech, freeodm of religion, the right to a fair trial, and protection against discriminaiton — though the exact list vareis somewhat between different countries' constitutions. Amendign or restricting a fundamental right is usually made deliberately difficult, often requirnig a special constitutional amendment process rahter than a simple majority vote in the legislature, precisely because these rigths are meant to be insulated from the shifting preferences of whichever poiltical party happens to be in poewr at a given moment.
